question: If God is autonomous, why would his will unfold as harmful to others?
premises: Good and bad deeds are distinguished by their fruits.
One might attribute this distinction to God's will alone.
An autonomous God would then be responsible for adopting a will that harms others.
inference: Attributing moral differentiation to God's autonomous will raises the problem of divine cruelty.
plain_english: If that division is made, does only his will unfold there? If he is autonomous, why would he adopt a will of his own that causes harm to others?
